newsitem.title: LEBANON: Solidere cancels shares worth $170 mln.
newsitem.headline: Solidere cancels shares worth $170 mln.

text.p: Shareholders in Lebanon's biggest company Solidere agreed on Monday to cancel shares worth $170 million, reducing the real estate firm's capital to $1.650 billion, a company spokesman said.
"An extraordinary shareholders' assembly today decided to cancel a number of A shares which represented buildings which Solidere gave back to their original owners," Rashid Fayed told Reuters.
"This brought down the company's capital to $1.650 billion from $1.820 billion," Fayed added.
Solidere A shares are those distributed to former holders of property rights in central Beirut which was damaged in the 1975-90 civil war and which Solidere is rebuilding.
The company's capital also includes B shares issued in a $650-million subscription in January 1994.
